_about: B2a step B agent report (workflow wf_64ae2038-fad, 2026-10-14).

b.summary:
I finished step B of B2a (the JS consumers, plus the one Python change), and every gate passes. Timelines served as engine_version 1 draw exactly what they drew before. I checked this beyond code reading: I rendered HEAD's stage and the working tree's stage side by side in jsdom, render mode, frame by frame. Over 32 B1-shaped timelines (12,280 frames), the frame keys and the whole stage DOM are identical. engine_version 2 timelines now draw the stored tokens. Against B1 they differ only in the owner-decision palette slots, and only on the colour-block chapter card and the crossfade out of it.

**Item 1: catalogue and roles (core.js)**
- core.js is now the only module that reads catalogue.gen.js, and it reads geometry only.
  - ZONES is rebuilt from the catalogue in B1's key order and frozen all the way down. Its JSON text equals B1's literal.
  - ROLES and the new BLOCK_ROLES come from `CATALOGUE.roles`.
  - TYPE_FLOORS and `templateSlots(id)` are new.
- `makeRoles` now offers the block roles through `color()`: `block.base`, `block.highlight`, `block.ink`, `block.ink2` and `scrim`.
  - Each one is the look's stored token when that field is present and valid, checked field by field and never by engine_version.
  - Otherwise it is B1's run-time derivation, computed lazily with the same maths. I moved that maths into core.js and kept `blockColors`/`blockColor` (colour_block.js) and `blockInk2`/`BLOCK_INK2_CONTRAST` (stage.js) as re-exports or wrappers.
  - The card surface was already read from the stored token.
- These places now read the roles: colour_block's colours, the Slot's block ink and ink2 (stage.js), and board_generic's title-block scrim.
- `roles.on(mode)` returns the scene's own roles for its mode. For the other mode it returns the `presentation.content_alt` content palette with the scene's structure roles, and throws when that palette is missing, incomplete or of the wrong mode.
- Unknown roles still throw.

**Item 2: preflight fixes**
- `fixesOf(look)` in core.js reads the fixes channel first and B1's legacy fields second.
  - A slot's size is the fixes value when it is a positive number, otherwise the legacy one.
  - A scrim, or the safe layout, holds when either channel asks for it.
- board_generic's `slotTuning` uses it. MIN_TEXT and MIN_LABEL come from TYPE_FLOORS and BODY_WEIGHT from the catalogue's body slot, so no literal floors are left. A JS test pins LAYOUT against the catalogue slots.
- Python `apply_remedies` now writes only `look.fixes`. The two legacy writes are gone; `look_is_safe` still reads `variant == "safe"`.
- The stub stage applies exactly the same rule.
- A new test shows that a remedied B2-resolved timeline never carries variant "safe".

**Item 3: template contract**
- types.js now defines TemplateModule, MediaOptions and FocusRect.
- board_generic implements:
  - `focusRect`: `{rect, shape:'rect', radius}`, edges rounded to whole px. Targets are `<item>`, `<item>:<part>`, `option:<i>` and `panel`/`panel:...`.
  - `itemEl`: the card body, so `.rt-k` spans are kept.
  - `dimGroups` and `anchor` (which returns null).
  - static `mediaBox`: B1's `mediaBoxMax`, plus slot `figure` for the 1200 x figureMax figure box.
  - static `tex`: B1's exact field list.
- stage.js gained `mediaBoxOf(scene, zones, mode, slot)`. Both `mediaPlan` and `ctx.media(ref, {slot, start, alt, box?})` use it, so a clip's box always comes from the hook. A picture may pass its own box.
- `ctx.timeline` is gone. `ctx.chapter` (state.js `chapterTitleAt`, same rule as B1) carries the kicker's chapter title.
- `kickerOf` is now `kickerOf(scene, chapter)`.
- aadhi/compose/motion/chunks.py needs no change:
  - its `_kicker_chapters` already hashes this exact title for the shown and outgoing scenes;
  - every timeline field the stage reads is in the chunk key;
  - the existing test still passes.

**Item 4: engine version and TeX**
- engine.js is a new module with no imports: `ENGINE_VERSION = 2`, `engineVersion`, `engineProblem`.
- The render page rejects `ready` with `timeline_invalid` before loading any font. `createDynamicStage` and the live player's `load()` refuse the same way, with `code: 'timeline_invalid'`.
- `timelineTex` is now the union of each scene's template `tex()`.
- The render page converts TeX through `pageTexRenderer`: one conversion per string, clones handed out, a cache that never evicts.
- `aadhiStage.texConversions()` is additive and counts conversions started after `ready`. A test shows it stays 0 on a TeX fixture.

**Item 5: source scan**
New rules, each with self-tests that must catch and must pass:
- Templates may not write will-change, filter, backdrop-filter, outline or text-decoration through any of these paths:
  - style properties, `setProperty`, `Object.assign`, CSS text;
  - the Painter's `style` and `attr`;
  - `h()`/`svg()` style objects and SVG attributes;
  - `setAttribute`.

  A property name the scan cannot read is refused in templates.
- Templates may not read `.timeline`, directly or by destructuring.
- Only core.js may import the catalogue, and nothing may read its `families`, `content`, `personalities` or `cues`.
- catalogue.gen.js must be data only.
- dynamic.css may not declare those properties, except its one measured will-change.

**Item 6: tests**
The new catalogue.test.js and the additions to the other test files are listed under tests. Two Python tests that read JS source text also had to change, because the JS they point at moved: test_templates.py (floors) and test_themes.py (derivation constants).
b.contracts:
**web/js/dynamic/engine.js (new; no imports, no DOM)**
- `ENGINE_VERSION = 2`.
- `engineVersion(timeline) -> number`: `presentation.engine_version` when it is an integer >= 1, otherwise 1. Same reading as Python `built_engine`.
- `engineProblem(timeline) -> string | null`: null when the version is <= 2; otherwise "the timeline was built by look engine N; this page draws up to 2 (reload to update it)".

**web/js/dynamic/core.js** (the only importer of catalogue.gen.js; geometry only)
- `ROLES = CATALOGUE.roles.colour`: same 14 names, same order as B1.
- `BLOCK_ROLES = CATALOGUE.roles.block`: `['block.base','block.highlight','block.ink','block.ink2','scrim']`.
- `ZONES`: built from `CATALOGUE.zones` in B1's key order, boxes `{x0,y0,x1,y1}`, frozen all the way down (B1 left the inner boxes and arrays unfrozen).
- `TYPE_FLOORS = CATALOGUE.type.floors`, with a TypeFloors typedef.
- `templateSlots(id) -> slot -> format -> variant -> SlotSpec`, or null for an id the registry does not list (an own property only), with a SlotSpec typedef.
- Moved here from elsewhere:
  - `BLOCK_INK2_CONTRAST = 3` and `blockInk2(ink, bgs)`, from stage.js;
  - `SCRIM_ALPHA_HEX = 'c7'`, from board_generic.
- `makeRoles(presentation, look) -> Roles {mode, tokens, color(role), inkOn(bg|bgs), on(mode)}`
  - `color()` accepts ROLES and BLOCK_ROLES and throws RangeError "unknown colour role" for anything else.
  - Block roles are computed lazily and field by field. Each is the stored `look.tokens` value when it is valid #RRGGBB (`scrim`: #RRGGBBAA). Otherwise:
    - base: dark families mix the accent 38% toward bg, light families keep the accent;
    - highlight: base mixed 35% back toward the accent (dark), or 10% toward white (light);
    - ink: `inkOn([base, highlight])`;
    - ink2: `blockInk2(ink, [base, highlight])`;
    - scrim: `${tokens.bg}c7`.
  - `on(mode)`:
    - the scene's own mode returns these same roles;
    - the other mode returns roles with the content palette of `presentation.content_alt` and the scene's structure and block roles, made once;
    - it throws RangeError when content_alt is missing, lacks one of the 9 content keys, or is of the wrong mode;
    - any other mode value throws RangeError "unknown colour mode".
- `fixesOf(look) -> {safe: boolean, slots: {slot: {size: number|null, scrim: boolean}}}`
  - The fixes channel is read first, B1's `text_fit` / `variant` second.
  - size: `fixes.slots[slot].size` when it is a positive number, otherwise `text_fit[slot].size`.
  - scrim: either channel is exactly `true`.
  - safe: `fixes.safe === true` or `variant === 'safe'`.

**web/js/dynamic/state.js**
- `chapterTitleAt(timeline, start) -> string`: the last chapter of `Timeline.chapters`, in array order, whose start <= start + 1e-3; '' when there is none. This was board_generic's kickerOf loop.

**web/js/dynamic/stage.js**
- `TEMPLATES` is typed `Record<string, TemplateModule>`.
- `templateFor` now looks up own properties only.
- `mediaBoxOf(scene, zones, mode, slot) -> {w, h}`: the template's `mediaBox(scene, zones, mode, slot, fixesOf(look))`, or the full stage when the hook is missing or returns an invalid box.
- `mediaPlan(f0, f1)` uses `mediaBoxOf(..., 'render', entry slot)`.
- `ctx.media(ref, {slot?, start?, alt?, box?})`: a clip's box always comes from `mediaBoxOf(scene, zones, stage.mode, slot)`; a picture may pass a valid `box` of its own.
- TemplateContext has no `timeline`; it gains `chapter`.
- Re-exports `BLOCK_INK2_CONTRAST` and `blockInk2` from core.js.
- `createDynamicStage` throws TypeError with `code: 'timeline_invalid'` in two cases:
  - a classic timeline (same message as before; the code is additive);
  - a newer look engine.

**web/js/dynamic/templates/types.js**
- Typedefs: TemplateContext (chapter, media: MediaOptions, no timeline), MediaOptions, FocusRect `{rect:{x,y,w,h}, shape:'rect'|'ring'|'bar', radius}`, TemplateModule, TextEntry.
- TemplateModule:
  - `{id, build, layout?, update, texts?, focusRect?, itemEl?, dimGroups?, anchor?}`;
  - static `mediaBox?(scene, zones, mode, slot, fixes)`;
  - static `tex?(scene, look, fmt)`.

**web/js/dynamic/templates/board_generic.js**
- `MIN_TEXT = floors('text_min')`, `MIN_LABEL = floors('label_min')`, both from TYPE_FLOORS.
- `BODY_WEIGHT` from `templateSlots('board_generic').body[fmt].default.weight`.
- `SCRIM_ALPHA_HEX` is re-exported from core.js.
- New constants: `CARD_RADIUS = 24`, `FRAME_RADIUS = 28`, `FIGURE_BOX_WIDTH = 1200`, `FIGURE_SLOT = 'figure'`.
- Signature change: `kickerOf(scene, chapter: string)`.
- `texOf(scene)` is new.
- Default export (annotated `@type TemplateModule`) adds:
  - `focusRect(ctx, target)`: whole-px edges; radius CARD_RADIUS, or FRAME_RADIUS for `panel`;
  - `itemEl(ctx, itemId)`: the card body;
  - `dimGroups(ctx)`: `[titleBlock, frame?, ...cards in page order]`;
  - `anchor(ctx)`: null;
  - `mediaBox(scene, zones, mode, slot, _fixes)`: `{1200, figureMax}` for slot `'figure'`, else `mediaBoxMax(scene, zones, mode)`;
  - `tex(scene, _look, _fmt)`: `texOf(scene)`.
- The scrim colour is `roles.color('scrim')`, and `slotTuning` uses `fixesOf`.

**web/js/dynamic/backgrounds/colour_block.js**
- `blockColor(roles)` is `roles.color('block.base')`.
- `blockColors(roles)` is `{base, highlight}` from the roles.

**web/js/dynamic/render.js**
- `timelineTex(timeline)`: the union over scenes of `templateFor(scene).tex(scene, look, fmt)`, first occurrence kept.
- `pageTexRenderer(convert) -> {renderTex, markReady(), conversionsAfterReady()}`: a page-wide cache that never evicts, returns clones, and drops a failed or throwing conversion so the next mount retries it.
- `boot`:
  - refuses a newer engine with RenderError `timeline_invalid` before fonts load;
  - uses one pageTex both for pre-conversion and as the stage's `renderTex`;
  - `window.aadhiStage.texConversions()` is additive: it throws not_ready before `ready`, then returns the number of conversions started after `ready`.
- STAGE_VERSION stays 3.

**web/js/player/player.js**
- `load()` rejects synchronously-before-build with TypeError `code: 'timeline_invalid'` for a live or preview Dynamic timeline of a newer engine.
- It now imports `../dynamic/engine.js` statically.

**Python, aadhi/compose/dynamic/preflight.py**
- `apply_remedies` writes only `look.fixes` (safe / `slots[slot].size` / `slots[slot].scrim`); `variant` and `text_fit` are never touched.
- `look_is_safe` / `safe_scenes` still read both channels.
- `SAFE_VARIANT` is now read only.

**Stub stage (tests/compose/dynamic/stub_stage/stage.js)**
- Applies the `fixesOf` rule exactly. `STUB.channel` still limits it to one channel.

**Source scan (web/tests/dynamic/sourceScan.test.js)**
- New rule ids: `template-style`, `timeline`, `catalogue`, `catalogue-data`.
- New exports: `scanStyleCss(text, file)` and `scanCatalogue(text, file)`.
- `scanCss` gains a `templateStyle` option.

**Test fixture (web/tests/dynamic/_fixture.js)**
- Exports `R1_PALETTES` (`[{name, stored ten tokens from the catalogue, b1 vector}]`), `OWNER_DECISION` and `STAGE_VECTORS`.

- midnight_indigo slot 0: block.ink2 #f2e5ea -> #F6EDF1.
- midnight_indigo slot 2: block.ink2 #f4e4e5 -> #F8EDEE.
- deep_teal slot 0: block.ink2 #eae7f2 -> #F1EFF7.
- paper_ink slot 2, the R-54 red lowering:

  - block.highlight #cc593d -> #BA6853;
  - block.ink2 #f8dbd3 -> #F2DDD7;
  - block.ink unchanged at #FFFFFF.

Where these show:
- ink2 is the kicker and subtitle on a colour block, and the ink preflight reads for them. The kicker's reported scrim background follows the block.
- The base and highlight are the colour_block fill and gradient.
- So only colour_block scenes (chapter cards and hooks) change, plus the crossfade out of them, where they are painted as the outgoing scene.
- The W2 families named in the decision (forest_night 1, cosmic 2 and 4, bold_blocks 0) differ the same way once released; R1 never resolves them.

Everything else an engine_version 2 look stores equals the B1 stage's value:
- the five B1 tokens, the scrim, and block.ink in all 12 R1 slots;
- block base, highlight and ink2 outside the slots above.

The only difference is hex letter case: stored values are upper case, B1's run-time mixes lower case. Pixels are identical. A Painter frame key can differ between a v1 and a v2 build of the same lecture because the hashed style strings differ in case. mesh_drift scenes draw the same keys and DOM (tested).

Evidence for the v2 claims:
- A DOM test in stage.test.js covers all 12 R1 family/slot pairs and confirms the drawn colours differ from B1 exactly by OWNER_DECISION.
- In the jsdom differential (HEAD vs working tree, 24 v2 timelines), the case-insensitive DOM differed only for deep_teal/0, midnight_indigo/0, midnight_indigo/2 and paper_ink/2, only on scene 1 (the colour-block chapter card) and scene 2 frames 420-432 (the crossfade out of it), in both formats.

b.open_items:
1. **mediaBox ignores fixes.** board_generic's static mediaBox keeps B1's boxes exactly (`mediaBoxMax`), so every frame key stays the same as B1's.
   - A title size cap below LAYOUT's title minimum (from fixes or `text_fit`) makes the drawn title shorter than `mediaBoxMax` assumes, so a clip can show up to about 3% larger than it was extracted. This is B1 behaviour, unchanged.
   - B2c's `media_split` should size its box from the `fixes` argument.
2. **Unplanned media.** These gaps are B1's, unchanged:
   - media.js `sceneClips` plans only the main clip and a video panel. A figure (`scene.figures`) that is a video, or a video poster, still has no planned frames and fails with `media_frame` in render mode. Its box keeps B1's values through `mediaBox` slot `figure`.
   - `mediaPlan` also lists a panel clip that board_generic does not show when a main clip exists (extra frames only).
3. **No morph anchor.** board_generic's `anchor()` returns null. B2f defines the shared-anchor morph and should bypass the fallback template.
4. **Code-editor surface missing.** `roles.on(mode)` gives the other mode's content palette with the scene's structure roles. The dark code-editor surface colour itself (`themes.code_surface`) is not in the timeline, so B2f must store it before code_walkthrough can draw it.
5. **ctx fields not added.** The plan §1.4 context fields `ctx.motion` and `ctx.outgoing` are not added yet (B2c, no consumer).
6. **Scanner limits.** It cannot see:
   - aliases (`const s = el.style; s.filter = ...`), `Reflect.set` or `Object.defineProperty` on a style;
   - an alias of CATALOGUE (core.js is the only importer, and that is pinned);
   - CSS from stylesheets other than dynamic.css.

   Unreadable style or attribute names, and dynamic imports with a computed specifier, are refused.
7. **Counter not read by the worker.** stage_page.py does not read `aadhiStage.texConversions()` yet. The gallery (B2g) should assert 0 per fixture, as plan §2 asks.
8. **Classic player imports engine.js.** player.js now imports web/js/dynamic/engine.js statically: one tiny module with no dependencies, added to the classic player's module graph. Classic output is unchanged (invariance green).
9. **Player error message.** For a newer-engine timeline the live watch page shows its generic "This lecture could not be played" message. A "reload the page" message would fit better (UI follow-up).
10. **Stale Python docstrings.** themes.py and colour_math.py docstrings name "colour_block.js blockColors" and "stage.js blockInk2 / BLOCK_INK2_CONTRAST" as the homes of the run-time derivations. Those names still exist as wrappers and re-exports, but the maths now lives in core.js `makeRoles`. I did not edit them (outside my scope).
11. **Two Python test edits outside item 2.** tests/compose/dynamic/test_templates.py (the floors check now pins the core.js route instead of looking for "CATALOGUE" in board_generic.js) and test_themes.py (the derivation and constant pins now read core.js). Both were needed because the JS they read moved.
12. **One-time cache miss.** The new engine.js and the core.js change alter `bundle_digest`, so motion chunk caches miss once after deploy (expected).
13. **Frame keys are not compared across engine generations.** A v2 build of a lecture can have different frame keys from a v1 build (upper- vs lower-case hex in hashed style strings) while the pixels are identical. Deduplication works within one render, so nothing breaks; do not compare keys across generations.
14. **Malformed engine_version is drawn as 1.** An engine_version that is not an integer is read as 1 (drawn), matching the API's `built_engine`, rather than refused. The schema forbids such values anyway.
